newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rate higher amid tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rate higher amid tight liquidity.

text.p: * Central Bank raises overnight lending to 15 percent
Manila overnight money shot up to an average of 12.28125 percent on Tuesday from 11.625 after the Central Bank raised its overnight lending rate to 15 from 13 percent, traders said.
Considering the tightness in liquidity caused by a long weekend covering, "the Central Bank's action was meant to encourage lenders to lend," a dealer said.
"It gave lenders leeway to increase rates," said another.
"The only fundamental reason the Central Bank did this was to control liquidity by discouraging banks from relying on the Central Bank as a last resort of liquidity," another dealer said.
Dealers said the Central Bank's net dollar sales late last week effectively also drained liquidity from the system.
Done rates jumped to a high of 15 percent, with the low at 11.375 percent. Volume fell to 24.064 billion from 26.647 billion pesos.
Out of the 61 participating financial institutions, 33 were lenders.
In secondary market for T-bills, banks were trying to sell their T-bills to generate peso liquidity, dealers said.
One dealer said the three-month bill was quoted an offer rate of 11.50 percent; the six months at 12; and the one-year at 12.575.
